heroHeadline: UK's MAST Upgrade Sets Record Plasma Pressure; MIT Proposes 'Economic Q' Viability Framework; ORNL Licenses Fueling Tech to Type One Energy
heroSubtitle: A research-heavy stretch for fusion after July's funding wave: UKAEA announced on August 6 that its MAST Upgrade spherical tokamak completed a fifth experimental campaign at Culham, generating 1,100+ plasmas and reaching the highest plasma pressure in the machine's history without destabilization, while suppressing disruptive Edge Localised Modes through four independent methods including a world-first use of 3D magnetic coils. On August 5, Oak Ridge National Laboratory licensed four cryogenic pellet-fueling technologies — including a tritium-compatible pellet gas gun and screw extruder — to stellarator developer Type One Energy, addressing a key gap in continuous D-T fueling for its Infinity One prototype. On August 10, MIT professors Dennis Whyte and Andrew Lo published a ten-parameter 'Economic Q' framework in the Journal of Fusion Energy for assessing commercial viability across any reactor concept, and California's Fuse Energy Technologies reported its FAETON-X dense plasma focus device hit a peak yield of 1.27 trillion D-D neutrons per shot — the company's claimed highest publicly documented neutron yield by any private fusion company, pending independent peer review. Global private fusion investment remains above $15 billion following July's record CFS and Helion rounds.
footerNote: Data sourced from DOE/LLNL/NNSA, ITER Organization, Commonwealth Fusion Systems, Helion Energy, Pacific Fusion, UKAEA, ORNL, ARPA-E, UK Government, Fusion for Energy, ANS Nuclear Newswire, peer-reviewed journals (Nature, Physical Review Letters, Journal of Plasma Physics, Journal of Fusion Energy, Fusion Science and Technology), and the Fusion Industry Association. All milestones independently verified.
